newsitem.title: Mexico: Mexican Feedlot Assn awaits dumping demand outcome.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Feedlot Assn awaits dumping demand outcome.

text.p: Mexican Feedlot Association still awaits the outcome of a request for the government to investigate imports of beef from the United States that they allege entered the country at dumping prices.
Enrique Lopez, the association's director, told Reuters the association expected the government to come out with a favorable decision and for the dumping investigation to start in coming weeks.

"We handed over the study to the Trade Ministry in April," Lopez said in a telephone interview. Ministry officials said it would take 30-35 days for the government to decide whether to investigate or not.
The association's allegations surround both imports of live cattle and meat at prices lower than those in the United States in 1996, Lopez said.
"We are showing that dumping does exist with official figures and confidential information," he added.

Lopez said according to original billing information in the association's possession kilo cuts of utility meat entered Mexico at prices between 8 and 9 pesos against a price equivalent to 24 pesos in the United States.
